scope: Two route-free official MCP SDK 2.3.1 runs against a checksum-verified unsigned experimental Debian 12 amd64 package. After the 1000-call process-hour budget was exhausted, the client submitted 16 guarded calls concurrently; accepted decisions and pre-execution capacity rejections were distinguished.
tested_package_manifest: SHA256SUMS from exact-main CI run 42213373890; all three files verified before testing
reproduce: Install pinned SDK with npm ci --prefix tools/mcp-sdk-probe --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund; set OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_DIR to that directory, OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_PACKAGE to the verified .deb, OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_PACKAGE_SHA256 to its 64-character digest, then run bash tools/netns_adversarial_probe.sh target/debug/outbound-guard-mcp twice.
checks: Each SDK burst result is either an EGRESS_RATE_LIMIT structured tool denial or a MCP_INPUT_BUSY protocol error for a request the server says was not executed. Accepted results have unique consecutive correlation IDs after the preceding serial decision, match the final audit events as a set across ID/status/rule, and contain no body. If no burst call is accepted, audit is unchanged. A subsequent serial denied call has the next ID and exactly matches the audit tail; tools/list stays responsive. No burst or recovery call caused DNS or HTTP. Package installation, hash/version, uninstall/residue and container/namespace cleanup passed.
harness_correction: An initial probe assumed all 16 concurrent calls would return structured tool decisions; the bounded input queue instead produced MCP_INPUT_BUSY protocol errors. The probe was corrected to assert that these pre-execution rejections do not consume an audit ID, while accepted decisions match audit and serial recovery works. A transitional assertion requiring both result kinds in every run was removed because the ratio is schedule-dependent. No server code changed.
local_verification: Two checksum-verified installed-package route-free suites passed 3384 and 3380 decisions. 47 Rust tests, 19 Python tests, cargo build --locked --bins --examples, cargo fmt --check, Clippy, JS/Python syntax, JSON parse and diff checks passed.
limitations: One SDK client, one process, finite 16-call submission bursts, one experimental Debian package/OS/architecture. Client-side concurrent submission does not prove simultaneous server execution or completion ordering under slow calls, general queue or resource bounds, cross-client/process behavior, traffic through other tools, official candidate or platform qualification. Owner self-review and residual-risk acceptance remain outstanding; independent human review is optional and was not performed. Four AI Scraping Defense repositories require separate adversarial evidence.
